detail:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) describes treatment for ADHD in children and adolescents as including behavior therapy and medications, with recommendations that vary by age group. CDC reports that the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends parent training in behavior management as the first line of treatment for younger children, before medication is tried, and describes behavior therapy as helping reduce problem behaviors and build self-regulation skills.

For children 6 years of age and older, CDC describes the recommendations as medication and behavior therapy together, including parent training for children up to age 12 and other behavior therapy and training for adolescents. Medicine classes described by CDC are stimulants, described as the best-known and most widely used ADHD medications, and non-stimulants. CDC notes that effective treatment plans include close monitoring and follow-up, with changes made along the way by the clinician when needed.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing ADHD, behavior therapy, and medicines.
sourceName: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
summary: CDC describes ADHD treatment as behavior therapy and medication varying by age, with parent training in behavior management first for younger children and a combination of medication and behavior therapy recommended for children 6 and older.
takeaways: behavior therapy comes first for younger children, cdc describes
for ages 6 and older, sources describe medication and behavior therapy together
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Managing ADHD day to day
